region: Östergötland, on the plain south of Lake Roxen
description: Ekeby is an old noble estate on the fertile Östergötland plain: a white manor house with two wings at the end of an avenue of limes, a home farm, its own mill, and some twenty tenant crofts scattered along the forest edge whose holders owe the estate days of labour. The present owner, a baron, spends the winters in Stockholm and has begun to replace the crofters with contract labourers (statare) paid in kind.
seasonNotes: April, the spring thaw. The snow has gone from the fields but lies grey in the forest; the roads are axle-deep in mud and almost impassable. Meltwater fills every ditch and the stream runs loud and brown over the mill weir. The first lapwings and larks return over the fields. Ploughing waits for the ground to dry; the crofters are spreading manure and mending fences. Easter falls this month.
travel: From Uppsala by rail to Stockholm, by the trunk line to Katrineholm, by the Southern Main Line to Mjölby (or by the eastern line to Norrköping and then by coach), and the last miles in a hired carriage or the estate's carriage over the thaw-mud roads: about a long day in April.

knownFor: One of the old noble estates of the fertile Östergötland plain, held by the same family since the 1600s
A fine manor library that scholars from Linköping and Uppsala sometimes ask leave to visit
A mill that grinds for the whole parish, and a large tenant system still run on days of labour

authorities.police: The crown sheriff (kronolänsman) of the Roxen plain district lives at Mjölby, about 20 km away; the parish has a constable (fjärdingsman) who answers to him and the vicar, and in practice to the steward.
authorities.court: The häradsrätt for the Roxen plain sits at Linköping, with a judge and twelve lay assessors; ordinary sessions are held a few times a year, and the parish is summoned by the sheriff.
authorities.doctor: The provincial doctor lives at Mjölby, 20 km away, and covers many parishes on bad roads; he can be sent for by the estate's rider, and often arrives a day late. He signs the death certificates.
authorities.post: The parish post point at the inn or the parsonage has post by relay twice a week; Mjölby and Linköping have daily post by train.
authorities.telegraph: Nearest telegraph office is at Mjölby station, 20 km away; Linköping is also reachable. Ekeby itself has no wire, so messages go on by rider or carriage.
authorities.bank: Östgöta Enskilda Bank in Linköping lends to the estate and the mill; the parish sparbank serves the crofters and is open on fixed days at the parsonage.
authorities.newspaper: Östgöta Correspondenten in Linköping is the local paper, read at the manor and the parsonage; Norrköpings Tidningar comes to the manor by post.

routes.name: Rail via Katrineholm and Mjölby, then carriage

legs.cost: about 1 riksdaler third class, about 2 second class
legs.notes: Private line, open since 1866. Carry travelling bags by hand; heavier gear goes in the goods van and may be delayed.

legs.schedule: daily through trains with a change at Katrineholm
legs.notes: State trunk line via Södertälje and Gnesta. Katrineholm is where passengers change for Östergötland.

legs.schedule: daily trains on the Southern Main Line, via Linköping
legs.notes: Mjölby is the nearest station and the seat of the crown sheriff and the doctor. Passengers can also get off at Linköping and go by road.

legs.notes: The last miles run along the limes' avenue but the road is deep in thaw mud, and the carriage may stick or the horses be changed at the roadside inn.

routes.name: Rail to Norrköping, then coach and the estate's carriage

legs.schedule: one or two trains a day
legs.notes: The newest stretch of the eastern line, not in the period list of known lines; times are uncertain and the stretch may suffer delays after the thaw.

legs.duration: about 8 hours including a change of horses
legs.cost: about 5 riksdaler by coach, plus a tip to the driver
legs.schedule: post coach in the morning; otherwise hire at the town inn
legs.notes: Slow in April. The last miles are in the estate's carriage if sent for, otherwise on a farm cart from the parish inn.

journey.journeyScene: The trains run south through a country of grey ploughland, standing water and last patches of snow in the lee of the barns. Beyond the railway station the road is a brown river of mud, the carriage wheels throw it in lumps, and lapwings tumble over the wet fields. On the far side of Lake Roxen the ice is dark and rotten, and somewhere over the water a boom sounds like a distant gun. Then the avenue of bare limes opens ahead, and the white manor and its two wings stand at the end of it, with smoke from the mill and the long barracks by the home farm.

publicFacts: The baron's family has owned Ekeby since the 1600s; the present baron spends winters in Stockholm and is often away.
The estate's steward manages the farm and the crofts in the baron's absence and is not well liked.
Crofters at Ekeby owe three days of labour a week in summer and two in winter, with a horse.
The baron has begun replacing crofters with statare families living in a long barracks at the home farm.
Two crofts were pulled down last year when their tenants left for America.
Ekeby's mill grinds for the estate and for the parish farmers, who pay a toll in grain.
The parish church contains the burial vault of the baron's family.
Ekeby's library is said to be one of the finest in the province.

places.name: Ekeby Manor
places.ownerRole: the estate's owners, a family of the lesser nobility
places.description: The manor stands white and severe at the end of a lime avenue whose trees are still bare, with crows building in the tops. Meltwater gurgles in the gutters and the gravel forecourt is soft with mud. In the windows the shutters are still half closed against the winter. Inside, the house smells of wax polish, stove heat and old wood.

places.description: The home farm stands behind the manor, a big quadrangle of red-painted barns, stables and cowsheds enclosing a muddy yard. The statare barracks is a long low building at one side, with children playing in the slush. Dung heaps steam in the cold morning. The steward's voice carries across the yard.

places.description: Lyckan is a red croft on a rise at the forest edge, with a lilac bush beside the door still bare of leaves. The thaw has made a pond of the yard and planks are laid across it. A cow and a pig shift in the byre. The crofter's wife is boiling washing in a pot over a fire outside.

places.name: Ekeby Mill
places.ownerRole: the miller, who leases the mill from the estate
places.description: The estate mill is a solid stone building on the stream below the manor, roaring with the spring flood. The weir is hidden under a curtain of brown water, and spray fogs the air. The miller has opened every sluice to spare the dam. Inside, the floor trembles with the wheel.

places.name: Ekeby Church
places.description: The parish church is a white medieval building on a mound in the fields, with the baron's family chapel built onto the north side. Snowdrops have come up in the churchyard among the old stones. Inside, the family's coats of arms hang on the walls. The bell rings for Easter with a sound that carries across the wet fields.

places.description: The parsonage is a comfortable yellow house a short walk from the church, its garden bare and wet. The vicar is a scholar who corresponds with the university in Uppsala. Crows walk in the ploughed glebe land. Inside, a fire is lit in every room against the spring damp.

places.description: The estate smithy stands by the road at the edge of the home farm, busy with ploughshares and harrow teeth for the coming spring work. Mud is trodden in and out of the open door. The smith is a crofter who pays his rent in iron work. The forge glow is warm in the grey April day.
